cards.explanation: The answer is staff, friends. The soldiers put it in His right hand, and a little later they take it and strike Him on the head with it. I think the robe, the crown and the staff together are meant to look like a king's outfit, and it's all for mocking. This part is heavy.

The answer is “Hail, King of the Jews!” friends. The soldiers kneel down and say it. The words sound like honor, but the text says plainly they were mocking Him. Notice the title they use. Keep it in your pocket, because it shows up again on the sign above His head.

The answer is own, friends. After they've mocked Him, they remove the robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they lead Him away to crucify Him. Hold onto that detail, because those same garments get divided up by casting lots in verse 35.

The answer is carry the cross of Jesus, friends. Along the way the soldiers find Simon, a man from Cyrene, and force him to carry it. The text says forced, so that word is doing the work. I think that's a heavy thing to be handed.

The answer is False, friends. Matthew says they offered Him wine mixed with gall, “but after tasting it, He refused to drink it.” So He tastes it, and then He refuses to drink it. Tasting and drinking are two different things, and the text keeps them apart.

The answer is one on His right and one on His left, friends. Two robbers are crucified with Him, one on His right and the other on His left. That puts Jesus in the middle. One robber is on each side of Him.

The answer is come down from the cross, friends. The people passing by say, “If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!” They say it while heaping abuse on Him and shaking their heads. They also say He's the one who was going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days.

The answer is believe in Him, friends. The chief priests, scribes and elders say, “Let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.” It's a mocking offer, and they say it as they stand there mocking Him.

The answer is deliver, friends. The chief priests, scribes and elders say, “Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him.” They also quote Him as saying, “I am the Son of God.” Those are their words, and they say them while mocking.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, “In the same way, even the robbers who were crucified with Him berated Him.” So the two men beside Him speak up too. That's the last mocking voice in this passage, and it's a heavy one.
